consensus_findings.description: Critical: `openspec/schemas/provider-model-map.schema.json` remains v2 provider→single `tierEntry` and is cited as the contract for agent-archetypes.3/4, but D14 plus skill-workflow.3 require exact agent-harness + dispatch-kind ordered ModelSpec chains (arrays), which today's schema cannot express—and live configs already need distinct CLI vs SDK chains (e.g. claude-remote, codex-remote).

Critical: Tasks 4.7–4.9 characterize, re-resolve, and delete `agents.yaml` model/`model_fallbacks` fields, but no requirement or task SHALL migrate/seed those existing primary+fallback values into the new `archetypes.yaml` per-(agent, dispatch_kind) chains before removal—so flag-off / pre-change parity (agent-archetypes.1, model-routing.14) has no data-migration owner.

Critical: When `ROUTING_ADAPTIVE` is on, OpenAPI `select_model` returns a single `Candidate` plus scored `alternatives` (no thinking, no ordered capacity chain), while agent-archetypes.4 / skill-workflow.2 require capacity retries to advance only within the harness+dispatch-kind `ModelSpec` chain from `archetypes.yaml`—the plan never defines how adaptive primary selection composes with that static capacity chain.

Critical: Task 3.10 implements `ROUTING_ADAPTIVE` delegation with D2's archetypes-owned static fallback before tasks 4.7–4.9 create harness-aware chains and remove agents.yaml models (4.7 even depends on 3.11→3.10). Until ownership lands, 3.10 either contradicts D14/D2 by still reading agents.yaml/ambient defaults, or depends on chains that do not yet exist.

Nit: `SelectModelRequest` omits `agent_id` / `dispatch_kind` (and `Candidate` omits thinking), yet D14 static fallback and discovery injection are harness- and dispatch-kind-specific; without these fields the HTTP/MCP select path cannot return a correctly scoped archetypes chain or preserve thinking levels.

Nit: Tasks 4.8–4.9 and wp-model-config-ownership require migrating discovery, coordination-bridge, and vendor_health off agents.yaml models, but skill-workflow/agent-archetypes only state negative constraints (no models in agents.yaml)—there is no SHALL that discovery/bridge responses expose the resolved archetypes chain or that health reporting must not invent ambient models.
Nit: `wp-probes` description/title still say tasks 6.1–6.6 while write_allow and tasks include 6.7–6.8 quota probe, and verification `-k 'probes or tripwires'` will not match `test_quota*`.
The amended plan establishes a coherent composition boundary from task and archetype tier to exact harness and dispatch-kind model chains, while keeping dynamic catalog selection separate.
The three-step test-first migration covers the existing sync CLI, async CLI, SDK, local discovery, API bridge, retry, and health consumers before removing legacy model fields.

Static model-policy ownership is cleanly separated between agents.yaml (harness identity, eligibility, transport, credentials, endpoint metadata, and invocation mechanics such as model_flag) and archetypes.yaml (sole curated authority for exact agent-harness + dispatch-kind ordered ModelSpec chains), delegating dynamic candidate selection to the coordinator catalog.

Tasks 4.7-4.9 and wp-model-config-ownership establish a safe migration sequence (characterization, versioned route resolution, and consumer migration) covering sync CLI, async CLI, SDK, discovery, bridge/API, and health consumers without reliance on ambient defaults.
Work-package DAG dependencies, file/key locks, write scopes, and verification steps across all 8 packages are fully specified, acyclic, and parallel-safe.

Cedar policy rules enforce hard feasibility constraints—such as subscription EULA programmatic-ineligibility and data residency floors—prior to scoring, ensuring non-compliant models are excluded before candidate ranking.

The 2-second resolver timeout and ROUTING_ADAPTIVE feature flag guarantee deterministic fallback to static archetypes.yaml model chains without ambient harness defaults or central coordinator single-point-of-failure lock-in.

The usage dashboard (apps/usage-viz) and telemetry correctly surface success-adjusted cost-per-completed-task per model x task-type as the primary comparison metric, supported by OpenTelemetry coordinator signals and estimate labelling.
Nit: Phase 6 task numbering in tasks.md places task 6.6 after tasks 6.7 and 6.8, resulting in a minor non-sequential task label ordering.

Nit: agent-archetypes.1 and model-routing.14 say flag-off must equal/restore “pre-change” static behavior, which conflicts with the intentional BREAKING storage move unless read as behavioral equivalence after migrating chains into archetypes.yaml.

Optional: Cross-file missing-route / orphan-harness validation failures are required to fail before dispatch, but no requirement emits a structured signal/metric for those configuration errors (unlike resolver timeout fallback).

FYI: D13’s optional quota-axi path shells out via `npx -y quota-axi` against local provider credentials; the plan correctly marks it read-only and off-by-default, but implementers should pin/verify the package and keep credentials out of argv/logs.

The D14 split is coherent: agents.yaml keeps harness mechanics including model_flag, archetypes.yaml owns curated ModelSpec chains, adaptive catalog stays dynamic-only, and wp-model-config-ownership is correctly serialized behind wp-resolver and wp-dispatch with non-overlapping parallel lanes elsewhere.

The 4.7→4.8→4.9 test-first sequence (characterize sync/async/SDK/discovery/health, then versioned resolution, then remove legacy fields and ambient defaults) is the right migration shape for eliminating dual model authorities without a big-bang cutover.

Fallback resilience is well specified at the control-plane layer: ROUTING_ADAPTIVE default off, >2s/error fallback, additive migrations, metered ceiling fallback to subscription/local, and quota probe degrade-to-reactive.
